page.layout: One page of running text, full width, with no margin notes. Page number and running head at the top. The text is in paragraphs, with a numbered paragraph 8 and 9 and a final paragraph whose number-led line starts with "1.".

main_text.p: um in promptu habemus, quæ de locis contro-versiis sensum suum nobis aperit: cujus judicio qui se submittere nolit, profectò se nullo judicio præditum esse offendit, & vix hominis nedum Christiani nomine dignus erit; qui enim omnem veteris & Catholicæ Ecclesiæ fidem derogat, nul-lam sibi relinquit. Æquissimi enim habendi sunt arbitri, nulloque partium studio in trans-versum abripi possunt, qui longè retroactis seculis ante lites & controversias nostras exortas vixerunt, sacrumque depositum, quod ipsi à majoribus per manus acceperant, fideliter nobis relique-runt.

8. Utilissimum itaq; gravissimumq; erat Decretum Concilii Viennensis sub Clemente 5 cele-brati, ut in Academiis essent linguæ Hebraicæ, Arabicæ, & Chaldaicæ Professores publici; qui linguas istas docerent, & libros ex ipsis in lin-guam Latinam transferrent, ad fidei propagati-onem, & infidelium faciliorem conversionem.

9. In seculo hoc nostro, quo literæ humaniores quasi revixerunt, maximo Ecclesiæ commodo & cum æterno ipsorum honore laborarunt viri longè doctissimi in editionibus Bibliorum, unà cum ver-sionibus quibusdam antiquis; inter quas præter Bombergi editiones plures Venetiis, Buxtorfii Basileæ, Vatabli Parisiis, Munsteri, Hutteri & aliorum, maximè eminent, & palmam reliquis eripuerunt, 1. Complutensis, 2. Antuerpi-ensis, 3. nupera Parisiensis.
1. Complutensis labore ac studiis Theologorum quorundam Complutensis Academiæ, impensis verò Cardinalis Ximenii Archiepiscopi Toletani, sex voluminibus comprehensa Anno 1510. in lucem prodiit,

page.notes: The scan is slightly blurred in places. The reading "Clemente 5" is uncertain: the numeral may be V with a superscript mark, and I have not marked it with [?]. The word "quæ" at the start of the second line is read as printed. Accent forms and ligatures in the Latin are copied as they appear. Long s is written as plain s, so "Munsteri" has no umlaut in print as far as I can see.
